title: Database Connectivity Concepts
subtopics: Choosing between embedded and server databases
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of database connectivity concepts in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply database connectivity concepts in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to choosing between embedded and server databases and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Database Connectivity Concepts through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding database connectivity concepts helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Database Connectivity Concepts helps you reason about database drivers and adapters. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Database drivers and adapters. Then connect it to Connection lifecycles. The remaining syllabus points—Configuration and credentials, Choosing between embedded and server databases—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Database Connectivity Concepts
content_blocks.code:
require "sqlite3"
db = SQLite3::Database.new(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE TABLE tasks (id INTEGER, title TEXT)")
db.execute("INSERT INTO tasks VALUES (?, ?)", [1, "Learn Ruby"])
puts db.get_first_value("SELECT title FROM tasks WHERE id = ?", 1)
db.close

content_blocks.title: Guided example

content_blocks.title: Recap
